reviewedChanges.area: Dependency graph and Expo API compatibility
findings: Production module and standalone encoder select the same three direct Media3 1.11.1 dependencies. The resolved graph verifier checks every resolved androidx.media3 component, requires common/effect/transformer/exoplayer, and rejects any mismatched version. No force/exclusion rule hides an incompatible component.

The Expo 3.0.16 config plugin is Android-only. It requires the exact original or adapted SHA-256, exactly one occurrence of each reviewed signature, and the exact resulting SHA-256. Only PlayerId arguments are added to getAllocator and shouldContinuePreloading; reversing those substitutions reproduces the complete original Java class.

Independent disposable-package tests execute the plugin action, test idempotence and unchanged iOS registration, and reject unknown package versions/source modifications. Owner retained actual Java counterfactual and production/complete instrumentation Kotlin compile evidence hashes were verified without duplicating those compilations.
reviewedChanges.limit: The checked Gradle configuration is debugRuntimeClasspath in the native compile/standalone encoder gates. Full UI builds assembleRelease; this review does not claim a fresh release-graph receipt or complete application compilation.

findings: Independently decoded all 90 packet metadata records from the exact fixture with FFprobe and verified presentation timestamps/keyframe flags against the checked-in method fixture. Asset SHA is bound.

All three retained upstream full-file SHA-256 values and exact method text match the fixture. The Java regression executes those method bodies with explicit surrounding stream/format doubles and four clip ranges/two reorder bounds. It reproduces 42 versus 45 retained frames and the exact 1.900/1.933333/1.966667-second missing packets.

The actual Android instrumentation adds the same input as an asset, asserts real reordered packets and three tail B-frames, requires 45 output video-page frames and a <=40 ms transition gap, and decodes late-video/next-page colors. Existing duration/audio/pixel/lifecycle expectations remain.
reviewedChanges.limit: Method execution and successful owner compilation do not establish native codec output. The new instrumented case is not yet executed on this candidate.

findings: Display-size acceptance requires square pixels, at most one exact right-angle matrix, no rotate tag ambiguity, and an actual unscaled FFmpeg PNG decode of 720x1280. Scaling/shear/mirror/translation/ambiguous matrices and wrong decoded size are rejected.

Per-channel audio measurement explicitly selects the original output channel before mono analysis and independently checks the source fixture. It avoids correlated stereo downmix amplification without changing selected-volume limits. Both channels must meet the original signal/score/leak thresholds.

Cadence still requires at least 27 fps, strictly increasing finite timestamps, a maximum gap strictly below 100 ms and the original tail constraint. The retained baseline remains failed at its actual 133.333 ms gap. Sixteen nested Python cases include exact baseline-gap and wrong-volume/channel/geometry negatives.

The original failed title remains THE LONG WAY HOMEENTURES in the retained baseline; the controlled component/save test reproduces that suffix without claiming the failed run retained a caret position. Production title/save source is unchanged.

Both applicable flows require semantic longPress/Select All, delete the selected range once, type the intended title and compare copied field text exactly before Save. The persisted/reopened cover assertion remains required. No coordinate tap, timeout extension or skipped assertion is introduced.
Android and iOS production memoryMovieVersion constants remain exactly 0; the existing QA overlay behavior is unchanged.
reviewedChanges.limit: Long-press selection and copied TextInput value must still succeed in real Maestro on both operating systems. Controlled-source tests do not establish native menu/accessibility behavior.
